title: Date from which the Months of a Valuation Step-Down Are Counted
content:
The months a valuation of a Keyturn Vehicle Listing steps down over are counted from an anchor date, and the anchor date is the most recent of the things standing on the vehicle's condition record that show the vehicle was looked at.

1. Where a completed inspection stands on the vehicle's condition record later than the valuation standing there, the months are counted from the date of that completed inspection.

2. Where no completed inspection stands later than that valuation but an odometer reading does, the months are counted from the date of the most recent such odometer reading.

3. Otherwise the months are counted from the date of the valuation standing on the condition record.

### Reading the three clauses in order

The clauses are read in the order written, and the first that fits governs. A vehicle whose condition record carries a valuation dated in March, a completed inspection dated in May and an odometer reading dated in July is on the first clause, and the months run from the May inspection — the later odometer reading does not displace it, because the second clause is reached only where no completed inspection stands later than the valuation.

A vehicle whose record carries a valuation dated in March and an odometer reading dated in July, with the last completed inspection dated in January, is on the second clause, and the months run from the July reading.

A vehicle whose record carries a valuation dated in March with nothing later than it is on the third clause, and the months run from that March valuation.
